titleZh: Homburg终止与Escarda激光除草机器人合作
summaryZh: 荷兰进口商Homburg经过近两年测试后，决定终止与德国初创公司Escarda Technologies的合作，不再在荷兰和比利时代理其AI控制的激光除草机。该机器从未售出，性能、可靠性和易用性未达预期。Escarda在被柏林工业集团收购后曾计划扩大生产，但Benelux市场已无望。Homburg表示将继续专注于有实际价值的品牌和技术。
featuredReason: 该新闻展示了AI激光除草技术在商业化落地中的现实挑战，对智慧农业领域的设备选型与合作决策具有重要参考价值。

Homburg says goodbye to Escarda

 03-08 | News | News

LinkedInFacebookXWhatsAppPrint

Homburg tested the AI-controlled Escarda LaserWeeder for almost 2 years but ultimately decided against further cooperation with German manufacturer Escarda Technologies. Photo: Escarda Technologies

Homburg is ending its partnership with German start-up Escarda Technologies. As a result, the Frisian importer will no longer represent the AI-controlled laser weeders in the Netherlands and Belgium.

According to Homburg, the decision was taken after an extensive test period of around 2 years. Ultimately, the machines did not meet the requirements set by the company and its intended customers in terms of performance, reliability and ease of use.

The partnership began in April 2025, when Homburg introduced the Escarda LaserWeeder for the Benelux. The machine uses cameras, artificial intelligence and laser technology to control weeds without chemicals. In June 2025, Homburg demonstrated the system during the Akkerbouwdag in Lelystad.

Start-up fails to gain a foothold

According to Homburg sales manager Marijn van den Akker, the machine was ultimately never sold. “It is a start-up that was still establishing itself in the market. The machine has not been sold anywhere in the world,” he says. Homburg therefore based its assessment on its own practical trials and discussions with potential customers, not on experiences from end users. According to Van den Akker, the machine ultimately did not sufficiently meet the expectations of Homburg and the market.

Line through growth ambitions

The termination of the partnership comes shortly after Escarda had presented growth plans. Following the full takeover by Berlin Industrial Group (B.I.G.), the company announced in May that it wanted to scale up production and build an international dealer and service network. That has now been ruled out for the Benelux. Homburg says it will continue to focus on brands and technologies that, according to the company, offer demonstrable added value for the professional farmer.

translationZh:
Homburg正在终止与德国初创公司Escarda Technologies的合作。因此，这家弗里斯兰进口商将不再在荷兰和比利时代理这款AI控制的激光除草机。

据Homburg称，这一决定是在约两年的大量测试期后做出的。最终，这些机器在性能、可靠性和易用性方面未能达到公司及其目标客户设定的要求。

合作始于2025年4月，当时Homburg向比荷卢地区推出了Escarda LaserWeeder。该机器使用摄像头、人工智能和激光技术，在不使用化学品的情况下控制杂草。2025年6月，Homburg在莱利斯塔德的Akkerbouwdag期间演示了该系统。

**初创公司未能立足**

据Homburg销售经理Marijn van den Akker称，该机器最终从未售出。“这是一家仍在市场中立足的初创公司。该机器在全球任何地方都没有售出，”他说。因此，Homburg的评估基于自己的实际试验和与潜在客户的讨论，而非终端用户的经验。据Van den Akker称，该机器最终未能充分满足Homburg和市场的期望。

**增长雄心受阻**

终止合作之际，正值Escarda刚刚公布增长计划。在被柏林工业集团（B.I.G.）全面收购后，该公司于5月宣布希望扩大生产，并建立国际经销商和服务网络。现在，这一计划在比荷卢地区已告吹。Homburg表示，将继续专注于那些据公司称能为专业农民提供明显附加值的品牌和技术。
